memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the first day of the seventh month hold a sacred assembly and do no regular work. It is a day for you to sound the trumpets. As an aroma pleasing to the LORD, offer a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram and seven male lambs a year old, all without defect." - Num 29:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The seventh month opened with a day of trumpet blasts, a sacred assembly set apart for the Lord. The sound of trumpets was a call to attention, rousing the people to remember God and gather before Him. It marked the beginning of a holy season, a summons to turn their hearts toward heaven.

There is something stirring about a trumpet call. It cuts through the noise of ordinary life and demands to be heard. For Israel, this blast was a yearly wake-up call, a reminder not to drift through life forgetting their God. It gathered the scattered attention of the people and focused it on the Lord.

We should remember that this festival, like the offerings around it, belonged to Israel's ceremonial worship under the old covenant and is not binding on believers today (Col 2:16-17). Yet the call it sounds still speaks. We too need regular summonses to lift our eyes from the busyness of life and remember the God who made and saves us.

Scripture tells us that one day a final trumpet will sound, and Christ will return to gather His people to Himself (1 Thess 4:16). That is the great assembly toward which all these gatherings pointed. Let the trumpet of this ancient feast remind you to stay alert, to keep your heart turned toward the Lord, and to live ready for the day when the last trumpet calls His people home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What "trumpet calls" does God use to draw your attention back to Him?
2. Do you need to lift your eyes from busyness and remember the Lord?
3. How does the promise of Christ's return shape the way you live today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, cut through the noise of my life and draw my attention back to You. Keep me alert and ready, living in hope of the day when the final trumpet calls Your people home. Amen.
